source: Fresh official AWS documentation; not native observations or local emulator results

fixture_conventions.case_identity: Stable case label plus operation and input; sequence preserves actual execution order
fixture_conventions.dynamic_values: Native resource IDs, request IDs, timestamps and public IPv4 addresses are preserved, not replaced with invented deterministic values
fixture_conventions.resource_binding: aliases maps semantic names to exact owned identifiers; replay substitutes only its own allocated resources
fixture_conventions.responses: SDK-decoded outputs/errors and actual EC2 rawResponseBody; credentials and signed request headers are never retained
fixture_conventions.cleanup: Exact owned resource selectors and absence errors; terminated-instance provider history is explicitly not claimed erased
fixture_conventions.local_separation: No local execution is represented in these native fixtures; documentation-only limits are not synthetic captured errors

conclusions: Allocation belongs to the account until release, independently of its association.
Domain is vpc; standard remains an enum value in the API model but documentation does not establish current actual admission.
Default pool is Amazon IPv4; BYOIP, IPAM, CoIP, recovery and Wavelength are separate controls.
Network border group constrains where an allocated address can be used.
Specify either InstanceId or NetworkInterfaceId, not both; InstanceId requires exactly one attached ENI.
PrivateIpAddress selects a primary or secondary private address; omission selects primary.
Reassociation is automatic by default; AllowReassociation=false prevents moving an EIP already associated with another resource.
Associating to a target with another EIP disassociates that old EIP without releasing its allocation.
Repeated association is documented as idempotent, but remapping charges may apply; no unbounded replay is performed.
Cross-network-border-group association is disallowed.
Disassociates from an instance or ENI without releasing the allocation.
Documented as idempotent; native errors for arbitrary missing or stale association IDs must remain captured separately.
There is a documented publicDualStackDnsName/last-primary-public-address restriction; this IPv4 capture does not exercise it.
A nondefault-VPC EIP must be disassociated first; otherwise InvalidIPAddress.InUse.
Default-VPC release can auto-disassociate, but no default VPC is mutated by this probe.
Incorrect NetworkBorderGroup is documented to return InvalidAddress.NotFound.
After release an address may be allocated to another account; AuthFailure is documented for a subsequent release in that situation.
AllocationIds and PublicIps select EIPs, not auto-assigned ephemeral IPv4 addresses.
Documented filters include allocation-id, association-id, instance-id, network-border-group, network-interface-id, network-interface-owner-id, private-ip-address, public-ip, tag:key and tag-key.
Filter names and values are case-sensitive.
Moving a secondary private address to another ENI also moves its associated EIP.
Remapping is asynchronous; metadata confirms completion.
AllowReassignment is this operation's separate private-address control, not AssociateAddress.AllowReassociation.
Only secondary private addresses or delegated IPv4 prefixes can be unassigned.
This API page does not specify the EIP-dependent rejection code; the native capture supplies that boundary.
An ENI must be detached from its instance before deletion.
This API page does not specify whether an unattached ENI's EIP prevents deletion; the native capture supplies that boundary.
Auto-assigned public IPv4 addresses are not account-owned EIP allocations.
Stopping, hibernating or terminating releases the ephemeral address; starting allocates a new one.
Associating an EIP releases the ephemeral address; disassociating the EIP ordinarily assigns a new ephemeral address.
An additional ENI or a secondary private address with an EIP suppresses that new ephemeral assignment.
Primary/secondary private addresses and EIPs stay with a secondary ENI when detached or attached.
Default quota is five EIPs per account per Region; it is adjustable and not an assertion about this account's current configured quota.
Public IPv4 addresses are charged whether used or idle.
The capture never exhausts quota and does not synthesize an AddressLimitExceeded observation.
Stopped instances retain their ENIs, private IPv4 addresses and associated EIPs.
Only auto-assigned public IPv4 addresses are released by stop.
Each instance start has a minimum one-minute charge; capture uses one instance repeatedly, never a second instance.
IPv4 internet access requires a public address and an attached IGW route for the destination.
A public address alone does not enable communication from a private subnet without an IGW route.
The IGW performs one-to-one NAT; the guest is aware of its private address rather than the translated public address.
This capture deliberately does not install an IGW route and makes no packet-reachability claim.
Gateway.NotAttached requires attaching an IGW before associating an EIP to a VPC ENI or instance.
DryRunOperation and UnauthorizedOperation are the permission-check results documented by the five public address APIs.
DryRun does not prove actual allocation, state validation or mutation; operation-specific native precedence must be taken from paired capture rows.
InvalidInstanceID is documented for operations that require an ENI selector on a multi-ENI instance.
InvalidNetworkInterface.InUse or InvalidParameterValue can describe an attached ENI deletion rejection.
